title: Lacto-Fermented Carrots
subtitle: Crunchy, slightly sour fermented carrot sticks with dill and garlic
excerpt: Fermented carrots use a 2% salt brine. Raw carrot sticks go into the jar with garlic and dill, submerged in brine and fermented for 5 to 7 days. No vinegar. Crunchy, lightly sour, and probiotic.
sourceNotes: Eastern European fermentation tradition. Carrots are one of the most beginner-friendly vegetables to ferment, they hold their texture well and the natural sugars ferment predictably.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ferment 5–7 days at room temperature; refrigerate when sour to your taste.

glossaryTerms.definition: Fermentation by naturally occurring lactobacillus bacteria on the vegetable surface, producing lactic acid to preserve and sour the food.

content.text: ed carrots are one of the most straightforward ferments to make. Raw carrot sticks go into a jar submerged in a 2% salt brine,  no salt-and-squeeze method needed, because the carrots don't need moisture removed first. The brine is made separately and poured over. After 5 to 7 days at room temperature, the carrots are mildly sour and crunchy, with the dill and garlic worked into them. Makes one 1-litre jar.

items.prepNote: peeled and cut into sticks 1 cm × 8 cm
cold, non-chlorinated if possible (filtered or boiled and cooled)

content.text: Stir the salt into the cold water until fully dissolved. No heating needed. Chlorinated tap water can inhibit fermentation,  if your tap water is heavily chlorinated, leave it in an open jug for an hour, or use filtered water.

Put the dill sprigs and garlic in the base of a clean jar. Pack the carrot sticks in vertically,  tight enough that they hold themselves upright. Add the peppercorns. Pour the brine over, pressing the carrots down so all are submerged. The carrots must stay below the brine surface throughout fermentation; above the brine is where mould grows. Use a small bag of brine, a rolled cabbage leaf, or a clean stone to weigh them down.

Cover the jar with a cloth secured with a rubber band, or use a loosely placed lid. Leave at room temperature (18 to 22 °C) for 5 to 7 days. Check daily and press the carrots down if any have risen. Taste from day 5,  they should be lightly sour and still crunchy. Refrigerate when the flavour is right.

items.cause: Temperature too cold, iodised salt, or heavily chlorinated water.
items.fix: Move to a warmer spot. Use non-iodised salt. Boil and cool the water first if it is heavily chlorinated.

items.cause: Fermented too long at a high temperature.
items.fix: Refrigerate from day 5. Carrots hold their crunch better than cabbage but will soften after 10+ days at room temperature.

items.symptom: White film on the brine surface
items.cause: Kahm yeast, harmless but can add off-flavours.
items.fix: Skim and discard. Ensure carrots stay submerged at all times to minimise surface exposure.
Discard. True lacto-fermentation smells sour and slightly tangy, not rotten or unpleasant.

content.text: Refrigerate once fermented to taste. Keeps for 3 to 4 months in the fridge, submerged in brine.
